title: Thousands march in Barcelona for housing relief, clashes with police reported

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated against Spain's housing crisis, which was highlighted by a legislative defeat for emergency housing measures and an eviction.
tea.want: Demands included housing relief, a 50% reduction in rent limits, an end to short-term leases, and a halt to evictions.
tea.changed: Oct 5: Clashes erupted in Barcelona between protesters and police after a demonstration for housing rights, leading to arrests and injuries.

summary: Tens of thousands of people marched in Barcelona on October 5 to protest Spain's housing crisis, hours after Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called an early election. The demonstration, organized by the Tenants' Union of Catalonia and major trade unions, called for housing relief, including a 50% reduction in rent limits, an end to short-term leases, and an immediate halt to evictions. While the main march concluded peacefully, groups of individuals clashed with police, throwing objects and setting fires. Police responded with baton charges and dispersal operations, leading to arrests and injuries among officers.
response: Police engaged in baton charges and dispersal operations, responding to objects thrown by protesters and street fires. The Mossos d'Esquadra police force confirmed 13 arrests and reported 28 officers sustained minor injuries.

crowd.text: Around 120,000 people flooded the streets to demand measures against the housing crisis according to the organisers…

arrests.text: 13 people including a minor were arrested in the clashes last night

updates.text: Tens of thousands of people marched in Barcelona to demand housing relief after the government's emergency housing measures were defeated in parliament.
After the official demonstration concluded, groups of protesters clashed with police, throwing objects and setting fire to bins.
Police conducted baton charges and dispersal operations, with clashes continuing until midnight.
Authorities reported 13 arrests, including a minor, and 28 police officers sustained minor injuries during the unrest.
